block.title: Separating the glibc proof layers shortens Hello’s cold open
block.p: Hello now reaches its safety theorem through 1,045 glibc interfaces, down from 1,092. It used to load the startup proof of hi_atexit to split lifetime and pointer shares and construct a null pointer cell. Both programs now get those lemmas from a shared memory module.

Each cold run on swa started with an empty interface cache, a prebuilt Rocq 9.3 worker and twelve compiler slots. The operating system kept its filesystem cache. The middle column runs the previous Make scheduler on the new sources. The last column gives priority to ready interfaces with the longest chain of waiting files.

We followed the last prerequisite to finish at each step of the safety build. With Make, 46.6 s passed between successive compilers on that chain. With the new scheduler those gaps totaled 3.9 s. The estimates use the creation of each compiler log and the last write to its interface as the start and end of the job.

The library theorem now imports 181 interfaces, up from 176. With the compiled interfaces on disk, the median of three fresh workers was 2.22 s for the safety theorem and 1.62 s for the library theorem. The earlier medians were 2.23 s and 1.62 s.

The architecture checker previously counted 420 imports that crossed a layer boundary in the wrong direction. It now counts zero. The longest import chain to the safety theorem fell from 92 files to 71.
